You are a Python worker on a personal executive-assistant repository at /mnt/d_drive/repos/EA. Your working directory is a scratch task directory; use it only for ./notes.md. Build your module in the repository at that absolute path.

OWNERSHIP. You own exactly ONE new repository file: scripts/sources/linkedin_threads.py. Two other workers are editing this same checkout right now in their own files; if you touch anything outside your one file you will corrupt their runs and fail the check. Do NOT edit tests/ (every test there is frozen and hash-checked), do NOT edit scripts/sources/intake.py, do NOT edit anything under _config/, AGENTS.md or ROUTER.md, do NOT touch ~/.claude/skills/, do NOT run git commit, git push or git add.

NO NETWORK, NO SECRETS. Do not call any API, do not retrieve any credential, do not run the linkedin skill. Everything is provable offline against fixtures already in the repo.

THE PROBLEM, measured 2026-08-07. The LinkedIn `chats` endpoint returns conversation THREAD metadata, not messages. Across 25 real records, `name` was null on 23 and a string on 2, `subject` was present on 3, and no record carried a message body at all. Pushed through intake.py's generic `_label`, 22 of 25 records rendered unreadable, and intake's volume-without-content gate failed the source every single day. The gate was right. The adapter was wrong.

THE RULING. LinkedIn is a metadata-only source. It reports what the endpoint actually knows, and it says so in the scan itself so that a daily brief can never cite this source for an absence claim below thread level. You are NOT weakening the volume-without-content gate; you are emitting lines that ARE readable content.

BUILD scripts/sources/linkedin_threads.py exposing:

    lines_from_payload(raw: str, cap: int = 60) -> tuple[list[str], bool, str | None]

  - `raw` is the stdout of `linkedin.py chats --output json`. It may carry a human header line before the JSON, and the JSON may be an envelope dict or a bare list. Parse from the first structural character, and find the record list WITHOUT guessing envelope key names. The `_walk` function in scripts/sources/intake.py is the model to follow; read it.
  - Emit one line per record that has unread_count > 0 AND a non-empty name or subject. The line contains that name or subject and marks the thread unread.
  - The LAST line is ALWAYS a single summary line carrying three counts: total threads, unread threads, and how many threads carry no name and no subject. It must also state that this is thread metadata only and that message bodies are never read.
  - `cap` bounds only the per-thread lines. The summary line SURVIVES capping and its counts describe the SOURCE, not the lines shown. truncated is True when per-thread lines were cut.
  - The third tuple element is the degradation note from the repo's uniform (items, truncated, note) adapter shape. For this source it is None.

HARD ARCHITECTURAL RULE: this module is a PURE FORMATTER. It takes text in and returns lines. It must NOT import subprocess, requests, urllib or http.client, and must not reference the linkedin skill. A formatter that physically cannot reach the network is the structural guarantee that no DM body, no `messages` call and no `profile` lookup can ever happen here. AGENTS.md bans raw message bodies from this workspace; your module is that ban made unable to regress. Do not emit any opaque identifier (account_id, provider_id, attendee_provider_id) into a line: an id is not readable content and putting one in a line would defeat the very gate this lane exists to satisfy.

HOW TO VERIFY, from /mnt/d_drive/repos/EA, iterate until both pass:
  python3 tests/test_linkedin_threads.py
  python3 /tmp/claude-1000/-mnt-d-drive-repos-EA/16e106db-dbb9-44a1-936b-63218d06190f/scratchpad/check_lane.py --lane A

Read the full docstring at the top of tests/test_linkedin_threads.py first: it is the complete specification, including the exact tuple contract and the fixtures in tests/fixtures/intake/. The test currently reports one failure saying your module does not exist. If a sibling lane's test is red for a missing module, that is not your problem and the check ignores it.

STYLE. This repository's code carries dense WHY-comments naming the incident each rule prevents. Match that register. No new dependencies. Keep it small.

OUTPUT. After both commands pass, write ./notes.md naming what you built, how you found the record list without guessing key names, how the summary line survives capping, the final output of both commands, and any assumption you made.

OWNERSHIP. You own exactly ONE new repository file: scripts/sources/hubspot_engagements.py. Two other workers are editing this same checkout right now in their own files; touching anything outside your one file corrupts their runs and fails the check. Do NOT edit tests/ (frozen and hash-checked), do NOT edit scripts/sources/intake.py, do NOT edit anything under _config/, AGENTS.md or ROUTER.md, and above all do NOT edit ~/.claude/skills/hubspot/hubspot_api.py. That skill lives outside this repo, outside git, and other surfaces depend on it. Do not run git commit, git push or git add.

NO NETWORK, NO SECRETS. Do not call the HubSpot API, do not retrieve any credential. Everything is provable offline against fixtures already in the repo.

THE PROBLEM, measured 2026-08-07. The skill CLI's `engagements list` sends only `limit` and `after` as query params. HubSpot v3 therefore returns only the default properties: `hs_createdate`, `hs_lastmodifieddate`, `hs_object_id`. Fifty task records and thirty meeting records came back with nothing readable, intake's `_label` fell through to the object id, the redactor masked that to `[id]`, and the volume-without-content gate failed both sources correctly, every day. The same skill's DEALS path does request explicit properties and works, which is the proof this is a defect and not an API limitation.

THE RULING, and the fence. The fix is requesting properties. The FENCE is WHICH properties. Task bodies and meeting notes in this estate carry client-identifying and patient-adjacent detail, and neither the ingest redactor in intake.py nor scripts/gates/phi_scan.py detects a bare human name; both files say so in their own docstrings. The only control that works is structural: never request, never parse, never label the field that carries a patient name. This mirrors scripts/sources/books.py, which reads only the GrandTotal row because a customer row would be a patient.

  REQUEST for tasks:    hs_task_subject, hs_task_status, hs_task_type, hs_task_priority, hs_timestamp
  REQUEST for meetings: hs_meeting_title, hs_meeting_start_time, hs_meeting_end_time, hs_meeting_outcome
  BANNED everywhere, in the request and in any label path: hs_task_body, hs_meeting_body, hs_internal_meeting_notes, hs_note_body

BUILD scripts/sources/hubspot_engagements.py exposing:

    PROPERTIES: dict[str, list[str]]   # the two allowlists above, exactly
    build_request(engagement_type, limit, after=None) -> tuple[str, dict]
        # returns (url, params). Pure. No auth, no I/O.
    fetch(engagement_type, limit, after=None, http_get=None, key_loader=None) -> dict
        # resolves the API key via key_loader() INSIDE fetch, defaulting to the
        # hubspot skill's load_api_key imported lazily; performs the request via
        # http_get(url, headers=..., params=...) defaulting to requests.get;
        # returns .json() on HTTP 200 and otherwise raises RuntimeError naming
        # the status code. The error message must never contain the key.
        # Importing this module must have NO side effects: no key load, no
        # network, nothing at import time.
    task_label(rec: dict) -> str | None
        # None when hs_task_status == "COMPLETED": a closed loop is not an open
        #   loop, the same rule fathom_action already applies in intake.py.
        # "(unlabeled record)" when the subject is missing or blank.
        # otherwise the subject, plus the due date from hs_timestamp when present.
        #   Never a bare timestamp as the label, never an id.
    meeting_label(rec: dict) -> str | None
        # "(unlabeled record)" when the title is missing or blank; otherwise the
        #   title plus the start date when present. A meeting is NEVER dropped
        #   for being completed: a logged meeting IS the signal.
    main()   # CLI: --type {tasks,meetings} --limit N, prints the JSON envelope

THE SUBTLE RULE, and it is the one that matters most: a record with a missing subject must render "(unlabeled record)", NOT be silently dropped. If you drop them, fifty broken records become an empty-but-OK source, which is a properties regression wearing a quiet day's clothes. The zero-versus-broken distinction is core doctrine in this workspace. The frozen test checks this explicitly.

  python3 /tmp/claude-1000/-mnt-d-drive-repos-EA/16e106db-dbb9-44a1-936b-63218d06190f/scratchpad/check_lane.py --lane C

Read the full docstring at the top of tests/test_hubspot_engagements.py first: it is the complete specification, and tests/fixtures/intake/ holds both the broken metadata-only shapes and the fixed shapes with edge cases. The test currently reports one failure saying your module does not exist. A sibling lane's test failing for a missing module is not your problem; the check ignores it.

Two other workers are editing this same checkout right now in their own files; touching anything outside your two files corrupts their runs and fails the check. Do NOT edit tests/ (frozen and hash-checked), do NOT edit scripts/sources/intake.py, do NOT edit scripts/sources/money.py, do NOT edit anything under _config/, AGENTS.md or ROUTER.md, do NOT touch ~/.claude/skills/. Do not run git commit, git push or git add.

ABSOLUTE RULE, READ IT TWICE. You must never retrieve, print, log, echo, write, or otherwise cause a real credential value to exist anywhere you can see. Do not run the real `secret-get`. Do not run `secret-store`. Do not run the real intake, bill.com or Plaid adapters. Everything you build is proven against a STUB `secret-get` that the frozen test places on PATH in a tempdir. If you find yourself about to run a command that would resolve a real value, stop: that is the failure this lane exists to prevent.

THE PROBLEM, measured 2026-08-07. Three sources failed the 08:50 scheduled run reporting missing credentials. Every one of those credentials is in fact stored and present. The discriminating fact from that same run: the source that resolved successfully called `secret-get` with an environment variable SECRET_CALLER set naming the caller, while the source that failed called bare `secret-get` and, critically, swallowed the tool's stderr with `2>/dev/null || echo ""`. Its error path threw away the evidence, so a DENIED retrieval and an ABSENT secret produced identical messages and the wrong one was reported for months. bill.com and Plaid failed more simply: their adapters read environment variables that nothing in the pipeline ever set.

BUILD scripts/sources/vault_wiring.py exposing:

    resolve_env(caller: str, mapping: dict[str, str]) -> dict[str, str]
        # mapping is {ENV_VAR_NAME: vault-entry-name}. For each entry run the
        # `secret-get` executable with argv EXACTLY ["secret-get", <name>] and
        # nothing else, with SECRET_CALLER=caller present in the CHILD env.
        # Return {ENV_VAR_NAME: resolved value}.
        # On a nonzero exit raise RuntimeError carrying the ENTRY NAME, the EXIT
        # CODE, and an excerpt of the child's STDERR. Never the value.
        # Nothing happens at import time; resolution occurs only inside this call.
    BILLCOM_ENV: dict          # the four bill.com ENV_VAR -> entry-name mappings
    plaid_env(institutions: list[str]) -> dict
        # client id mapping, secret mapping, and one access-token mapping per
        # named institution

Surfacing stderr is the anti-regression clause and the single most important line in this module: swallowing it is exactly how a denied retrieval got reported as an absent secret. A RuntimeError that says only "failed" recreates the bug this lane exists to kill.

ALSO CREATE state/plaid_items.json: {"items": [{"name": ..., "token_env": ...}, ...]} for the institutions ameris, wise and capone. INSTITUTION NAMES AND ENVIRONMENT VARIABLE NAMES ONLY. No values of any kind. This file is committed to git, and a checkout of this workspace must carry no bank access whatsoever. scripts/sources/money.py's items() function already defines this contract; read it and match it exactly rather than inventing a shape.

The exact vault entry names you must map to are listed in the frozen test. Read them there. Do not guess them and do not go looking for them anywhere else.

OUT OF SCOPE, deliberately: scripts/sources/money.py passes a token to plaid_client.py on argv. That is pre-existing, it crosses into another skill, and it is the owner's decision. Do NOT fix it here and do not edit money.py.

  python3 /tmp/claude-1000/-mnt-d-drive-repos-EA/16e106db-dbb9-44a1-936b-63218d06190f/scratchpad/check_lane.py --lane D1

Run those as bare commands exactly as written. This machine has a file-read safety hook that refuses any shell command whose text combines a reader like grep, head, tail or cp with a path containing words like secret, key, token or credential; a bare python3 invocation runs clean. That hook is also why this module is named vault_wiring rather than something more obvious.

Read the full docstring at the top of tests/test_vault_wiring.py first: it is the complete specification. Note that its case 1 runs a deliberately leaky resolver through the same detector your real module faces, so the leak detector proves itself on every run. The test currently reports two failures: your module missing and state/plaid_items.json missing. A sibling lane's test failing for a missing module is not your problem; the check ignores it.
